chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Nawfali, from Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi, raising it (to the Prophet), said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to sit in three postures: Al-Qurfusa (squatting), which is that he raises his shins and faces them with his hands, and tightens his hand in his arm; and he used to kneel on his two knees, bending one leg and extending the other upon it; and he was not seen sitting cross-legged at all.

key_terms.الْقُرْفُصَا: A specific squatting posture where the knees are raised and the hands embrace them.
key_terms.مُتَرَبِّعًا: Sitting cross-legged, with one shin placed over the other knee.
key_terms.يَبْسُطُ: To extend or spread out (referring to the leg).

ai.seo_question: What were the specific sitting postures of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as described in Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) preference for the 'Qurfusa' (squatting with hands on knees) and the 'Tafarruj' (one leg bent, the other extended) postures, while explicitly noting his avoidance of the 'Mutarabb'' (cross-legged) position. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction is significant as it informs the recommended etiquette (Adab) of sitting during prayer and rest, distinguishing the Prophet’s unique practice from common cultural norms of the time. The narration underscores the importance of following the Sunnah in bodily postures as an act of worship and imitation of the Prophet’s humility.
